:
This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 25.12.2022 at about 11.30 a.m. petitioner had been riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08- SCCH-5 K-1462 carefully, cautiously by observing traffic rules and norms along with his wife Munivenkatamma near Anjaneyaswamy Temple,
Doddakadathur Village, Malur Taluk, Kolar, at that time, a motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-08-Y-2093 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motor cycle, as a result of which, petitioner and his wife fell down and sustained multiple injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Government Hospital, Malur after first aid, he was shifted to Gourav Orthopaedic Hospital, Kolar, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food, nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 54 years, hale and healthy, working as Governemnt SCCH-5 School Teacher, thereby drawing salary of Rs.68,171/- p.m.
Out of this accident crime No.14/2023 is registered against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-Y-2093 before the Malur Rural Police.
Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said offending motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.

4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition and further stated that, he is absolute owner of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-2093 and all the vehicle documents are standing in his name and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 vide its policy SCCH-5 No.14012192375001512 valid from 09.08.2019 to 08.08.2024.
Further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is very exaggerated.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further admitted issuance of policy of insurance bearing No.140121923750015512 valid from 09.08.2019 to 08.08.2024.
Further submitted that, the said offending vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident.
Further submitted that, there is delay of 20 days in lodging the complaint and he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, petitioner was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-K-1462 without holding valid and SCCH-5 effective driving licence.
Manjunath.
C vs Santhosh Kumar.

N on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37234172/
2
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side and rider of the offending motor cycle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further denied age,
nature of injury, period of treatment and amount spent towards treatment by the petitioner.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
6.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 14.01.2023 at about 4.00 p.m. when the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-K- 1462 near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Doddakadathur Village, Malur Taluk, Kolar, at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-Y-2093 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner SCCH-5 vehicle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, Record Section Keeper in Gourav Orthopaedic Surgical Hospital, Kolar is examined as PW-2, one eyewitness by name Shankarappa is examined as PW-3 and Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital is examined as PW-4 and marked 22 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.22 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced their evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
SCCH-5 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of re- statement is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
SCCH-5 Manjunath.C vs Santhosh Kumar.

N on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37234172/
3 10.

Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Record Section Keeper in Gourav Orthopaedic Surgical Hospital, Kolar as PW-2, one eyewitness by name Shankarappa is examined as PW-3 and Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital is examined as PW-4.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-4 and records those have marked i.e.,
FIR, complaint, re-statement, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 25.12.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.
SCCH-5

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 25.12.2022 at about 11.30 a.m. when he was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-K- 1462 near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Doddakadathur Village, Malur Taluk, Kolar.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-Y-2093.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the SCCH-5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture both bones of right forearm, for the said injury, he underwent surgery in the form of ORIF with DCP for fracture both bones.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 25.12.2022 to 29.12.2022.

He has also exhibited medical bills to the tune of Rs.56,566/- marked as Ex.P.12, medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.13, 3 photographs with 1 CD marked as Ex.P.14 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.15.
SCCH-5 14.

To substantiate his case, he has examined Record Section Keeper by name M.V.Srinivas in Gourav Orthopaedic Surgical Hospital as PW-2 and furnished copy of MLC Extract marked as Ex.P.17, admission card marked as Ex.P.18, case sheet marked as Ex.P.19 and authorization letter marked as Ex.P.20.
15.
Further Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring & Lady Curzon Hospital is examined as PW-4 and exhibited clinical report marked as Ex.P.21 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.22.
He also assessed total disability of the petitioner of right lower limb at 38% and whole body disability at 19%.

In the cross- examination PW-4 deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner Manjunath.C vs Santhosh Kumar.N on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37234172/
4 and he has no personal knowledge about injury and treatment taken by the petitioner.
Further deposed that, as per X-ray Films, now the fractures are SCCH-5 united, implants are insitu.
Further deposed that, he has not suggested the petitioner to Medical Board to issued disability certificate and himself also not issued disability certificate.
Further he has not issued estimation for requirement of Rs.40,000/- for removal of implants.

16. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 54 years, for proof of his age, petitioner has furnished copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.10, further he has furnished copy of driving licence marked as Ex.P.16 wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 03.05.1968 and the alleged accident is occurred in the year 25.12.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.16, his age is considered about 55 years as on the date of accident.
17. As per his case, petitioner was serving in Government School as a Teacher, thereby drawing salary SCCH-5 of Rs.68,171/- p.m.
To prove the said facts, he has furnished payslip for the month of December 2022 marked as Ex.P.11.

In cross-examination of PW-1 dated 16.02.2024, he has categorically admitted that, he was drawing salary of Rs.61,000/- p.m. as on the date of accident and now is drawing Rs.73,000/- p.m. that means, he is continuing his service as Government School Teacher.
Under such circumstances, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income on account of disability and loss of income during id up period.

18. Further during the course of arguments, respondent No.2 counsel Sri.HTV vehemently argued that, there is 2 days delay in lodging the complaint and said delay has not been proved and it is self fall accident with the collusion of the police, the case has been built SCCH-5 up and petitioner is Government Teacher and no future income is arise in this case and prays to dismiss the petition.
19.

Per contra, the counsel for the petitioner Sri.MVH resisted the said arguments and argued that,
this is case of head on collusion and due to bed ridden by the petitioner and his wife i.e., due to injuries sustained out of the accident, it takes sometime to lodge complaint and there is no rebuttal evidence on respondent's side and as per the IMV Report there is damage to both the vehicles and petitioner is Government Teacher and there is fracture to the right hand and prays to allow the petition.
As per the arguments of petitioner counsel, that means, except arguments and cross-examination of PW-1, respondents have not adduced any evidence.
SCCH-5 20
. Further admittedly he has exhibited copy of the medical bills amounting for Rs.56,566/- marked as Ex.P.12.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated i.e.,
Dr.Imran Hussain has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 25.12.2022.
So as per Ex.P.7 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained fracture to the both bones of right forearm, which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Sudeep for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-4 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in Manjunath.C vs Santhosh Kumar.N on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37234172/
5 SCCH-5 the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.56,566/-.
21.
Per contra, except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Further except cross-examining the PW-1 orally, they have not taken any steps to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
SCCH-5 22.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl
. No .
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Pain and sufferings 20,000-00 2. Conveyance, nourishment and 20,000-00 attendant charges 3. Loss of amenities in life 20,000-00 4.
Medical Expenses 56,566-00 Total 1,16,566-00 23.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,16,566/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.140121923750015512 which is valid for the period from 09.08.2019 to 08.08.2024 in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-Y-2093, the alleged accident was SCCH-5 occurred on 25.12.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of respondent No.1 shall go against respondent No.2, so that, respondent No.2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

25. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

6

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,16,566/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixteen Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH-5
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
